title: Low-Cost Decision Making for Group of Vehicles for Safe Mobility in V2X
summary: TCS Research reports that its AI framework for decisions by vehicle groups predicts quality of service better for following vehicles; no source reports a road trial or a safety or fuel result.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: In a preprint of 27 February 2024, researchers at Fraunhofer HHI, Ericsson Research and TU Berlin reported that measurements from prior vehicles can improve the prediction of quality of service for the vehicles that follow. By June 2025 TCS was researching low-cost decision making for groups of vehicles through virtual simulations. The TCS submission cites that preprint and describes the same result in close to the same words as its own finding. Safer traffic and lower fuel use remain intended benefits. In March 2026 the TCS Research authors Garima Mishra, Hemant Kumar Rath and Sai Bhavadeesh Yarlagadda presented the framework at the IEEE PerCom Workshops in Pisa. They report that measurements from a leader vehicle improve the prediction of quality of service for following vehicles. They report no road trial and no safety or fuel result.
purpose: Coordinate connected vehicles for safer and more efficient movement.
system: AI vehicle-group decision-making framework for V2X

evidence.citation: Garima Mishra, Hemant Kumar Rath and Sai Bhavadeesh Yarlagadda, Stationarity-Aware QoS Prediction for Platooning in V2X Networks, 2026 IEEE PerCom Workshops (Pisa), 16 March 2026. All three authors work at TCS Research and submitted the ITU use case. evidence.citation: Noor Ul Ain, Rodrigo Hernangomez, Alexandros Palaios, Martin Kasparick and Slawomir Stanczak, QoS prediction in radio vehicular environments via prior user information, arXiv 2402.17689, 27 February 2024. The authors work at Fraunhofer HHI, Ericsson Research and TU Berlin, none works at TCS, and the German research ministry funded the work through the AI4Mobile project. They published the method of using prior vehicles' measurements to predict QoS for following vehicles; the TCS submission cites the preprint as reference 6 and describes the same result in close to the same words as its own finding.
